items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the civil rights law and the civil practice law and rules, in relation to creating the right to be forgotten act
items.lawCode: Add §50-f, Civ Rts L; amd §215, CPLR
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4561

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the civil rights law and the civil practice law and
rules, in relation to creating the right to be forgotten act

 PURPOSE :

This bill mandates that upon the request from an individual, all
search engines, indexers, publishers and any other persons or entities
that make available, on or through the internet information about the
requester, shall remove information, articles, identifying information
and other content about such individual that is "inaccurate",
"irrelevant", "inadequate", or "excessive" within thirty days of such
request. The bill would rectify an individual's reputation that was
wrongly diminished through inaccurate information found on the
Internet.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 is amended by adding a new section 50-f in which mandates
that information regarding the individual that is "inaccurate",
"irrelevant", "inadequate", or "excessive" shall be removed.

Section 2 provides for either an action for actual monetary loss for
each violation or statutory damages in the amount of two hundred fifty
dollars after such removal request for each day of such violation to
the entity for not cooperating with section one in the duration of
thirty days after receiving a removal request.

Section 3 the Secretary of State shall oversee all right to be
forgotten requests, filings, takedowns and if applicable, any
penalties, judgments, costs and/or attorney's fees.

Subdivision 3 of section 215 of the civil practice law and rules is
amended and a new subdivision 9 is added to recover damages for
assault, battery, false imprisonment, malicious prosecution, libel,
except libel as defined under subdivision nine of this section,
slander, false words causing special damages, or a violation of the
right of privacy under section fifty-one of the civil rights law.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill seeks to rectify damaged reputations of individuals whose
lives have been affected through inaccurate information found online.
Currently, the statute of limitations provides that a person may sue
within one year of being defamed by a publisher. While this was
sufficient when publishing was limited to television and news print,
todays online publications can resurface in perpetuity through online
search engines. This bill would allow an individual to remedy their
situation when the damaging information is found to be inaccurate.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2017: A.5323 (Weprin)
2016: A.10466 (Weprin)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires search engines, indexers, publishers and any other persons or entities which make available, on or through the internet or other widely used computer-based network, program or service, information about an individual to remove such information, upon the request of the individual, within thirty days of such request.
title: Relates to creating the right to be forgotten act
